item.title: pCloud Pass Cyberattack Exposes Email Addresses and Triggers Login Attempts
item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Nov 07:00 → 28 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

pCloud Password Manager Hit by Cyber Attack Involving Email Address Exposure and Login Attempts — Should Read

pCloud Pass contained a cyberattack that exposed a small number of user email addresses and triggered login attempts, but says encrypted vault data, passwords, and notes were not compromised. Users should watch for phishing attempts seeking their master password or recovery words.

  • pCloud Pass said it promptly contained a cyberattack that exposed a small number of user email addresses and involved login attempts.
  • pCloud said passwords, notes, and other information stored in pCloud Pass were not compromised because they are encrypted and require a master password to access.
  • The incident was limited to pCloud Pass and did not affect pCloud Cloud Storage services, according to the company.
  • Users reported receiving new-device sign-in alerts for a device called "pd," including users who had two-factor authentication enabled.
  • pCloud urged users to watch for phishing messages that request their master password or recovery words through email, phone, or chat.

Technologies: secrets-manager, object-storage, mfa, source-control

Products: pcloud-pass, pcloud-cloud-storage, msecure, 1password, github

Vendors: pcloud, mseven-software, 1password, github

item.title: pCloud Pass breach confirmed as organizations weigh post-quantum cryptography readiness
item.content:encoded:
Window: 27 Nov 19:00 → 27 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

pCloud confirms password manager hack after suspicious login alerts — Should Read

pCloud confirmed that its pCloud Pass password manager was targeted in a contained cyberattack that exposed a small number of user email addresses and triggered suspicious login alerts, including for accounts protected by 2FA. The company says password vault contents were not compromised, but has not said whether encrypted vaults were accessed or stolen.

  • pCloud confirmed that a cyberattack targeting its pCloud Pass password manager was promptly contained.
  • The company said a small number of pCloud Pass user email addresses were exposed and login attempts were made, triggering automatic notifications.
  • Users reported alerts about an unfamiliar device named "pd" connecting from an IP address in Luxembourg, including some users with two-factor authentication enabled.
  • pCloud said its cloud-storage services were not affected and that passwords, notes, and other pCloud Pass data were not compromised because they are encrypted on customers' devices.
  • pCloud did not disclose whether encrypted password vaults were accessed or stolen during the incident and warned users to watch for phishing attempts.

Technologies: secrets-manager, mfa

Products: pcloud-pass

Vendors: pcloud

Preparing for the future AI cryptography break — Optional

Rumors of AI-driven cryptographic breakthroughs do not yet justify immediate changes, but organizations should inventory their cryptography and build algorithm agility now. This preparation will speed response to any future weakness in RSA or elliptic-curve cryptography and support migration to post-quantum, hybrid encryption.

  • Reports that AI labs may have results affecting deployed cryptography remain unconfirmed, and the article says they should be treated as a thought experiment rather than a reason for immediate changes.
  • A practical break of RSA-2048 or elliptic-curve cryptography could affect TLS connections, website certificates, and software signing, while current AI results against AES and cryptographic systems do not threaten modern deployed key sizes.
  • The article recommends that organizations create a cryptography inventory, design systems so algorithms can be replaced, and accelerate post-quantum cryptography migration using hybrid schemes where appropriate.
  • Aikido's CBOM feature is described as identifying cryptographic algorithms, protocols, and certificates in repositories, including use through libraries, while flagging weak algorithms such as MD5 and SHA-1.
  • NIST published its first post-quantum cryptography standards in August 2024, and the article states that a sufficiently capable quantum computer could also break RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography.

Products: aikido-dspm, aikido-attack-surface-monitoring, claude-mythos-preview

Vendors: aikido, anthropic, google-deepmind, google-research, nist

item.title: Cloud Breaches Hit Boston Scientific and Air Force as WeaveLotus Targets Southeast Asia
item.content:encoded:
Window: 27 Nov 15:00 → 27 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

US Air Force cloud platform reportedly hacked in latest federal breach — Should Read

Hackers reportedly breached the US Air Force’s Cloud One platform through an unidentified software flaw, potentially exposing sensitive military operational and logistics data. The incident is part of a recent wave of reported US federal breaches, though no attribution or confirmed data theft has been disclosed.

  • Hackers reportedly breached the US Air Force’s Cloud One computing platform after exploiting an unidentified software vulnerability.
  • The intrusion was discovered within the past month during a platform upgrade and disrupted application migrations and software updates.
  • Cloud One supports Department of Defense applications for military operations, personnel management, logistics, and maintenance, and the breach may have exposed sensitive operational and logistics information.
  • US Cyber Command is assessing the incident, while the attackers, scope of the intrusion, and whether data was stolen remain unknown.
  • The reported breach follows recent reported incidents affecting the FBI, CIA, ODNI, NGA, and the Treasury Department’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network.

Technologies: cloud-platform, backup

Products: cloud-one, artex, oracle-peoplesoft, connectwise-cloud-backup, microsoft-365

Vendors: us-air-force, oracle, connectwise, microsoft

Suspected Vietnam-Linked Hackers Target Southeast Asia in South China Sea Espionage Campaign — Should Read

SOCRadar identified a suspected Vietnam-linked espionage group, WeaveLotus, targeting Thai and Philippine government, military, and legislative systems to collect intelligence related to South China Sea defense interests. The group exploited exposed applications and default or weak credentials, then used reverse SSH tunnels and credential attacks to access and exfiltrate sensitive records.

  • SOCRadar identified a suspected Vietnam-linked activity cluster named WeaveLotus that targeted military, government, and legislative organizations in Thailand and the Philippines, with reconnaissance against Indonesian government organizations.
  • The RedOps campaign was observed from August to September 2026 and appears intended to collect internal government records and documents related to Vietnam's foreign-policy and military-intelligence priorities.
  • WeaveLotus gained initial access mainly through exposed web-application weaknesses and default credentials in GeoServer, JasperReports, osTicket, and Laravel debug-mode configurations.
  • The group used reverse SSH tunnels and SOCKS5 proxies to retain internal access and move into other networks and applications.
  • Confirmed intrusions included the extraction of hundreds of thousands of records from a Thai government-related downstream application and staff account data from a Philippine government organization's osTicket system.

Technologies: database, cms, identity-provider, iam, vpn, firewall

Products: geoserver, jasperreports, osticket, laravel, microsoft-sql-server, keycloak, directus, wowza-streaming-engine, globalprotect, connect-secure, cisco-asa, fortigate

New Boston Scientific data breach exposes personal, medical info — Should Read

Boston Scientific disclosed that a May 2026 vishing-driven breach of its cloud infrastructure exposed personal and health insurance information, including SSNs, for 117,789 people. The company says no patient medical records, connected-device systems, or product operations were affected, and the incident was unrelated to its separate August 2026 cyberattack.

  • Boston Scientific is notifying individuals after a voice-phishing incident gave an attacker access to the company’s cloud infrastructure.
  • The Texas Attorney General breach portal reports that 117,789 people had personal and medical information exposed, including Social Security numbers, government ID numbers, and health insurance information.
  • Boston Scientific said patient medical records and data from remote monitoring systems, connected medical devices, and clinical workflow applications were not exposed.
  • The company said the incident did not disrupt manufacturing, ordering, distribution, patient services, product safety, or device remote monitoring.
  • Boston Scientific confirmed that this incident is unrelated to the separate August 2026 cyberattack that caused global operational disruption.

Vendors: boston-scientific, crowdstrike

What Happened to Binance Can Happen to Any Fortune 500 Company — Optional

Constella’s analysis of a sample of Fortune 500 companies finds that widespread employee data exposure, infostealer-compromised credentials, and third-party breaches create the same conditions exploited in the Binance attack. The report argues that security teams must monitor exposure beyond their own incidents and treat supplier and identity risk as core attack surfaces.

  • Constella analyzed 63 confirmed breaches involving 62 Fortune 500 companies in its sample and counted 2.06 billion exposed records between 2013 and 2026.
  • Twenty-seven of the 63 breaches, or 43%, were attributed to suppliers, vendors, or third-party platforms, including 18 linked to the MOVEit file-transfer campaign.
  • Across 20 randomly selected Fortune 500 companies, Constella detected 6,598,492 corporate-email exposures in a 12-month period, including 316,554 employee identities in infostealer logs from 72,733 infected devices.
  • The report states that 96.2% of employee exposure in its 20-company sample originated outside the companies' own incidents.
  • Constella reported 18 ransomware or extortion cases in its sample, including 13 confirmed cases and five additional companies listed by the n0n group in November 2026.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: moveit, snowflake, salesforce

Vendors: constella-intelligence, snowflake, salesforce

Sponsored ISPsystem content argues that unmanaged virtual machines, orphaned access, and incomplete physical-infrastructure inventory create security blind spots that firewalls and other controls cannot solve. It promotes the ISPsystem stack as a centralized alternative for VM lifecycle management, physical inventory, access control, and resource accounting, particularly for organizations migrating away from VMware.

  • The article argues that firewalls, endpoint detection tools, backups, vulnerability management, and network separation are effective only when the underlying infrastructure is under control.
  • Virtual machines created without documented owners or lifecycle rules can be forgotten, miss updates and monitoring, and become possible entry points for attackers.
  • The article says centralized access management, role-based permissions, action logging, environment separation, and resource lifecycle control are needed to reduce excessive privileges and unmanaged resources.
  • It states that organizations migrating from VMware to alternatives such as Proxmox VE or OpenStack may need to separately integrate resource accounting, access control, equipment management, and inventory functions.
  • The sponsored article promotes ISPsystem's VMmanager, DCImanager, and BILLmanager as an integrated platform for virtual-machine management, physical infrastructure inventory, provisioning, quotas, accounting, and resource lifecycle workflows.

item.title: SAP Source-Code Incident and Vinci RAT Microsoft Store Abuse
item.content:encoded:
Window: 27 Nov 11:00 → 27 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

Microsoft Store App Found Delivering Vinci RAT Capable of Remote System Control — Should Read

A malicious Microsoft Store app called Setup Assistant was used to deliver Vinci RAT, giving attackers persistent remote control through obfuscated JavaScript and PowerShell payloads. The campaign used fake software download sites and a Microsoft-signed installer to lure victims before the app was removed from the Store.

  • Researchers at eSentire reported that attackers used a fake snipping-tool website to deliver a Microsoft-signed installer named Snipping-Tool.exe, which installed the Microsoft Store app Setup Assistant.
  • Setup Assistant, an Electron-based application published by ETPS Ltd., used obfuscated JavaScript to communicate with attacker-controlled infrastructure and execute PowerShell or JavaScript supplied by that infrastructure.
  • The campaign deployed Vinci RAT, which can identify the infected computer, check installed security tools, provide remote shell access, transfer files, and run shellcode, DLL, EXE, and PowerShell payloads.
  • A PowerShell stager disabled Windows AMSI, created a scheduled task that ran every 10 minutes, contacted monkeysholder[.]info, and downloaded the Vinci RAT payload.
  • The Setup Assistant app was no longer accessible in the Microsoft Store at the time of reporting, and eSentire said Microsoft had previously responded to its abuse report by stating that the app did not violate its terms.

Technologies: operating-system, remote-access

Products: microsoft-store, setup-assistant, windows, powershell, antimalware-scan-interface, electron

Vendors: microsoft, etps-ltd

Software giant SAP confirms cyber incident amid reports of source code breach — Should Read

SAP confirmed a cybersecurity incident involving suspicious activity in its GitHub-based development environment, with reports that stolen employee tokens may have enabled source-code access or modification. SAP says it has found no evidence that customer business data was accessed and has restricted development systems while investigating.

  • SAP confirmed it identified suspicious activity and took steps to protect customers and secure its services.
  • Reports said attackers targeted SAP’s GitHub-hosted software development environment using employee authentication tokens that may have allowed source code to be copied or modified.
  • SAP said its investigation had found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data.
  • SAP reportedly restricted GitHub access, halted automated development processes, and replaced digital keys used to verify software integrity.
  • It remains unclear whether proprietary source code was accessed or whether any altered code was delivered to customers.

Products: github

Japan’s education ministry discloses breach of government procurement system — Should Read

Japan’s education ministry said hackers breached its government procurement system, potentially exposing 164,000 business records and nearly 1,700 email addresses. MEXT isolated the system, reported the incident to data protection authorities, and says it has found no evidence of public disclosure or misuse.

  • Japan’s Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology detected an intrusion into its government procurement system on October 1 and disclosed it nearly two months later.
  • Hackers may have accessed the system’s database, potentially exposing nearly 1,700 email addresses and 164,000 records containing company names, employee names, and other business information.
  • The affected system publishes government tender, contract, and procurement opportunities, and the potentially exposed information concerns companies eligible to participate in the ministry’s bidding processes.
  • MEXT blocked communications between the affected system and internal and external networks and said it found no evidence that the potentially compromised information had been publicly disclosed or misused.
  • The ministry reported the incident to Japan’s data protection authorities and is continuing its investigation with relevant government agencies.

Microsoft will remove the WSUS server role from Windows Server 2028, though WSUS remains supported on earlier releases such as Windows Server 2025 for their support lifecycles. Organizations are being directed toward cloud-based update-management tools including Windows Autopatch, Microsoft Intune, and Azure Update Manager.

  • Microsoft recommends that organizations move client update management to Windows Autopatch and Microsoft Intune and server update management to Azure Update Manager.
  • Windows Server 2028 will also remove VBScript, WMIC, and Windows Internet Name Service (WINS) support.

item.title: Swiss AI-Assisted Critical Infrastructure Breaches and Cacti 4HTTP2SHELL Zero-Day
item.content:encoded:
Window: 27 Nov 03:00 → 27 Nov 07:00 UTC (4 hours)

Unpatched Cacti Zero-Day Enables RCE in Just Four HTTP Requests via Guest Access — Should Read

An unpatched zero-day in Cacti Core 1.2.31 lets unauthenticated guest users achieve remote code execution in four HTTP requests by chaining stored SQL injection with unsafe poller command execution. Until a fix is released, disable guest access, restrict web-interface exposure, and inspect poller configurations for suspicious commands.

  • A proof-of-concept zero-day, tracked as 4HTTP2SHELL and 4HTTP2ROOT, can enable unauthenticated remote code execution in Cacti Core 1.2.31 when the guest account is enabled.
  • The attack uses guest access to store non-numeric text in the preview_graphs_per_page setting, which is later used to execute arbitrary database queries when the graph preview page is loaded.
  • The demonstrated attack modifies a Cacti poller-table record and then invokes the realtime poller endpoint, causing the stored command string to be passed to PHP's popen() function without allowlist or sanitization checks.
  • The researcher identified four contributing failures: guest users can write arbitrary strings to a numeric setting, stored defaults bypass validation, the PDO driver permits stacked statements through a SQL LIMIT clause, and the poller executes database-stored command strings.
  • Until a fix is available, users are advised to disable the guest account, limit access to the Cacti web interface, and review poller configuration entries for unexpected commands.

Technologies: network-monitoring

Products: cacti-core

Vendors: cacti

Switzerland Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Breached Critical Infrastructure Operators — Should Read

Switzerland confirmed its first AI-agent-assisted intrusions, including successful breaches of critical-infrastructure operators, reflecting a wider European rise in autonomous attacks that exploit familiar weaknesses at far greater speed and scale. Authorities urge rapid patching, reduced internet exposure, strong authentication, and behavior-based monitoring.

  • Switzerland’s National Cyber Security Centre said AI agents breached systems in four of five confirmed recent attacks on Swiss organizations.
  • Three attacks targeted critical-infrastructure operators, and two succeeded without causing major reported disruptions.
  • Swiss authorities said agentic offensive frameworks can scan for known unpatched weaknesses, run attacks in parallel, and switch methods when defenses respond.
  • Italy’s CSIRT Italia reported that AI-directed autonomous agents compromised many systems within hours by combining vulnerabilities, configuration errors, and compromised credentials.
  • Swiss, Italian, and UK authorities recommended rapid patching, limiting internet exposure, strong authentication, and monitoring for unusual activity.

Products: artex, cyberstrikeai, pentagi, deepseek-harness

New NFS2ROOT Linux flaw can let attackers gain root privileges — Should Read

A critical 12-year-old Linux NFS server flaw, CVE-2026-99362 (NFS2ROOT), can let remote unauthenticated attackers gain root access when NFSv4.1 or v4.2 is exposed on TCP port 2049. Organizations should immediately update to a patched kernel and reboot, or restrict NFS access to trusted networks until patching is possible.

  • CVE-2026-99362, dubbed NFS2ROOT, is a critical heap buffer overflow in the Linux NFS server that can allow remote attackers to gain root privileges.
  • The flaw has existed since Linux kernel 3.16, released in March 2014, and affects systems running nfsd with NFSv4.1 or v4.2 when TCP port 2049 is reachable.
  • OpenSec disclosed that crafted NFS requests can corrupt kernel memory, defeat address randomization protections, and cause a command to run as root when the attacker closes the NFS connection.
  • Patched kernel versions include 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2, and 7.4-rc1, and administrators should update and reboot systems to use the fixed kernel.
  • No exploitation in the wild has been reported, but organizations that cannot patch immediately should restrict NFS TCP port 2049 to trusted clients or disable the NFS server if it is unnecessary.

  • SOCRadar identified a suspected Vietnam-linked activity cluster called WeaveLotus that conducted five confirmed intrusions against military, government, and legislative organizations in Thailand and the Philippines between August and September 2026.
  • The operators gained initial access chiefly through exposed web-application flaws and default credentials in GeoServer, JasperReports, osTicket, and Laravel deployments, then maintained access through reverse SSH tunnels.
  • In one Thai military intrusion, the attackers likely exploited CVE-2024-36401 in GeoServer, accessed Directus file records, performed text extraction on collected images, and attempted to access surveillance video feeds.
  • In a Thai government intrusion, the attackers obtained Keycloak credentials, cracked password hashes, and used valid accounts to retrieve 349,782 records from a downstream application.
  • The group also performed reconnaissance against more than 30 Indonesian government organizations, but SOCRadar said this activity did not advance beyond reconnaissance.

Technologies: vpn, firewall, proxy, cms, identity-provider, iam, database, remote-access

Products: geoserver, jasperreports-server, osticket, laravel, directus, keycloak, microsoft-sql-server, wowza-streaming-engine, globalprotect, ivanti-connect-secure, cisco-asa, fortigate

Vendors: socradar, geoserver-project, tibco, osticket, laravel, directus, red-hat, microsoft, wowza, palo-alto-networks, ivanti, cisco, fortinet

Software giant SAP confirms cyber incident amid reports of source code breach — Should Read

SAP confirmed a cybersecurity incident involving suspicious activity in its GitHub-hosted development environment, where attackers reportedly obtained employee tokens that may have enabled source-code access or modification. SAP says it has found no evidence that customer business data was accessed and has restricted GitHub access and rotated security keys.

  • SAP confirmed it identified suspicious activity and said it took immediate steps to protect customers and secure its services.
  • Reports citing internal communications said attackers targeted SAP’s GitHub-hosted software development environment and obtained employee authentication tokens that could allow them to copy and modify source code.
  • SAP said its investigation had found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data.
  • SAP reportedly restricted GitHub access, halted automated development processes, and replaced digital keys used to verify the authenticity of its software.
  • It remains unclear whether attackers accessed proprietary source code or whether altered code was delivered to customers.

Technologies: source-control, ci-cd

Products: github

Vendors: sap, github

Microsoft Store App Found Delivering Vinci RAT Capable of Remote System Control — Should Read

A malicious Microsoft Store app called Setup Assistant was used to deliver Vinci RAT, giving attackers persistent remote control through obfuscated JavaScript and PowerShell payloads. The campaign used fake software download sites and a Microsoft-signed installer to lure victims before the app was removed from the Store.

  • Researchers at eSentire reported that attackers used a fake snipping-tool website to deliver a Microsoft-signed installer named Snipping-Tool.exe, which installed the Microsoft Store app Setup Assistant.
  • Setup Assistant, an Electron-based application published by ETPS Ltd., used obfuscated JavaScript to communicate with attacker-controlled infrastructure and execute PowerShell or JavaScript supplied by that infrastructure.
  • The campaign deployed Vinci RAT, which can identify the infected computer, check installed security tools, provide remote shell access, transfer files, and run shellcode, DLL, EXE, and PowerShell payloads.
  • A PowerShell stager disabled Windows AMSI, created a scheduled task that ran every 10 minutes, contacted monkeysholder[.]info, and downloaded the Vinci RAT payload.
  • The Setup Assistant app was no longer accessible in the Microsoft Store at the time of reporting, and eSentire said Microsoft had previously responded to its abuse report by stating that the app did not violate its terms.

Technologies: operating-system, remote-access

Products: microsoft-store, setup-assistant, windows, powershell, antimalware-scan-interface, electron

Vendors: microsoft, etps-ltd

Switzerland Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Breached Critical Infrastructure Operators — Should Read

Switzerland confirmed its first AI-agent-assisted intrusions, including successful breaches of critical-infrastructure operators, reflecting a wider European rise in autonomous attacks that exploit familiar weaknesses at far greater speed and scale. Authorities urge rapid patching, reduced internet exposure, strong authentication, and behavior-based monitoring.

  • Switzerland’s National Cyber Security Centre said AI agents breached systems in four of five confirmed recent attacks on Swiss organizations.
  • Three attacks targeted critical-infrastructure operators, and two succeeded without causing major reported disruptions.
  • Swiss authorities said agentic offensive frameworks can scan for known unpatched weaknesses, run attacks in parallel, and switch methods when defenses respond.
  • Italy’s CSIRT Italia reported that AI-directed autonomous agents compromised many systems within hours by combining vulnerabilities, configuration errors, and compromised credentials.
  • Swiss, Italian, and UK authorities recommended rapid patching, limiting internet exposure, strong authentication, and monitoring for unusual activity.

Products: artex, cyberstrikeai, pentagi, deepseek-harness

Hackers Trojanize Official Q-Dir and DesktopOK Downloads to Deliver Remote Access Malware — Should Read

Official Q-Dir and DesktopOK installers and updates from SoftwareOK were reportedly trojanized to install a Python-based remote-access tool that can execute commands, steal files, and capture screenshots. Users of affected versions should check installer hashes and persistence mechanisms such as suspicious scheduled tasks, as reinstalling the apps alone may not remove the RAT.

  • AhnLab reported that official SoftwareOK downloads and updates for Q-Dir and DesktopOK were tampered with to install a Python-based remote-access tool.
  • Confirmed poisoned versions include Q-Dir 12.83.0.0, 12.84.0.0, and 12.85.0.0, as well as DesktopOK 12.82.0.0 and 12.85.0.0.
  • The malicious installer launches the legitimate application while downloading 7-Zip and a package containing the remote-access tool and its Python runtime from mail.c1a2[.]top.
  • The remote-access tool can run shell commands and Python code, transfer files, capture screenshots, and collect operating-system and system information after connecting to 8.210.69[.]51:9876.
  • The malware creates a scheduled task disguised as Microsoft Edge for persistence, and it checks running processes for numerous security products before sending the results to its command-and-control server.

Technologies: remote-access, operating-system

Products: q-dir, desktopok, 7-zip, python

Vendors: softwareok, ahnlab, 7-zip, python-software-foundation

pCloud confirms password manager hack after suspicious login alerts — Should Read

pCloud confirmed that its pCloud Pass password manager was targeted in a contained cyberattack that exposed a small number of user email addresses and triggered suspicious login alerts, including for accounts protected by 2FA. The company says password vault contents were not compromised, but has not said whether encrypted vaults were accessed or stolen.

  • pCloud confirmed that a cyberattack targeting its pCloud Pass password manager was promptly contained.
  • The company said a small number of pCloud Pass user email addresses were exposed and login attempts were made, triggering automatic notifications.
  • Users reported alerts about an unfamiliar device named "pd" connecting from an IP address in Luxembourg, including some users with two-factor authentication enabled.
  • pCloud said its cloud-storage services were not affected and that passwords, notes, and other pCloud Pass data were not compromised because they are encrypted on customers' devices.
  • pCloud did not disclose whether encrypted password vaults were accessed or stolen during the incident and warned users to watch for phishing attempts.

Technologies: secrets-manager, mfa

Products: pcloud-pass

Vendors: pcloud

New Boston Scientific data breach exposes personal, medical info — Should Read

Boston Scientific disclosed a vishing-driven cloud breach affecting 117,789 people in the United States, exposing personal identifiers, health insurance details, and medical information. The company says patient records, connected-device data, and product operations were not affected, and the incident is unrelated to its separate August 2026 cyberattack.

  • Boston Scientific said a caller using social engineering gained access to its cloud infrastructure, exposing cloud-based applications and hosted data.
  • The company became aware of unauthorized access on May 12, and its investigation determined that a data breach occurred on November 5.
  • The Texas Attorney General breach portal reports that 117,789 people were affected, with exposed data including names, addresses, Social Security numbers, government ID numbers, medical information, health insurance information, and dates of birth.
  • Boston Scientific said patient medical records and data from remote monitoring systems, connected medical devices, and clinical workflow applications were not exposed.
  • The company said this incident did not disrupt its operations or affect the safety, performance, or remote monitoring of its medical devices, and that it is unrelated to the August 2026 cyberattack.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Japan’s education ministry discloses breach of government procurement system — Should Read

Japan’s education ministry said hackers breached its government procurement system, potentially exposing about 164,000 business records and nearly 1,700 email addresses. The ministry has isolated the system and is investigating, with no evidence so far of public disclosure or misuse.

  • Japan’s Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology disclosed that hackers breached its government procurement system after detecting the intrusion on October 1.
  • The ministry said attackers may have obtained data from the system’s database, including nearly 1,700 email addresses and 164,000 records containing company, employee, and other business information.
  • The affected system publishes information on government tenders, contracts, and procurement opportunities, and the exposed business information concerns companies eligible to participate in ministry bidding processes.
  • MEXT blocked communications between the affected system and internal and external networks and said it found no evidence that the potentially compromised data had been publicly disclosed or misused.
  • The ministry reported the incident to Japan’s data protection authorities and is continuing its investigation with relevant government agencies.

Technologies: database

Microsoft removes WSUS server role in Windows Server 2028 — Should Read

Microsoft will remove the WSUS server role from Windows Server 2028, although WSUS will remain supported on earlier releases such as Windows Server 2025 through their support lifecycles. Organizations should plan to migrate update management to Windows Autopatch, Microsoft Intune, and Azure Update Manager.

  • Microsoft will remove the Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) server role from Windows Server 2028.
  • WSUS remains available and supported on earlier Windows Server releases, including Windows Server 2025, for each release's support lifecycle.
  • Microsoft says WSUS on supported earlier server releases can continue managing updates for supported Windows clients and servers, including Windows Server 2028.
  • Microsoft recommends Windows Autopatch and Microsoft Intune for client update management and Azure Update Manager for server update management.
  • Windows Server 2028 will also remove VBScript, the legacy WMIC utility, and Windows Internet Name Service (WINS) support.

Technologies: operating-system, iam, cloud-platform

Products: windows-server-2028, windows-server-update-services, windows-server-2025, windows-autopatch, microsoft-intune, azure-update-manager, windows-internet-name-service

Microsoft pushes emergency hotpatch to fix Windows Server crashes — Should Read

Microsoft released emergency out-of-band hotpatch KB5138318 for Windows Server 2025 to fix 0x139 crashes triggered when time-bound IPv6 route timers expire after the November 2026 hotpatch update. The fix installs automatically for affected hotpatch-enrolled servers without requiring a reboot.

  • Microsoft released out-of-band hotpatch KB5138318 to address Windows Server 2025 crashes caused by the November 2026 security hotpatch KB5131077.
  • Affected Windows Server 2025 devices with Router Advertisement enabled may stop with error 0x139 when a time-bound IPv6 route expires.
  • KB5138318 is rolling out automatically through Windows Update to affected Windows Server 2025 devices enrolled in hotpatch updates and does not require a restart.
  • Microsoft also reported that November 2026 hotpatch updates have caused application installation and launch issues on Windows 11 and printing issues for systems using Forcepoint’s DLP Endpoint Agent.
  • Microsoft said hotpatch security updates would be enabled by default for eligible Microsoft Intune- and Microsoft Graph API-managed Windows devices after the May 2026 security updates.

Technologies: operating-system, cloud-platform, dlp

Products: windows-server-2025, windows-11, windows-hotpatch, windows-update, windows-autopatch, microsoft-intune, forcepoint-dlp-endpoint-agent

British government takes services offline following ‘cyber incident’ — Should Read

The UK Department for Work and Pensions took some online services offline after an undisclosed cyber incident, while benefit and pension payments continue as normal. The agency is investigating with national cyber authorities and aims to restore services quickly.

  • The UK Department for Work and Pensions took some online services offline as a precaution after a cyber incident.
  • The department did not disclose the nature of the incident.
  • Regular benefit and pension payments are not affected and will be paid as normal.
  • The Department for Work and Pensions is working with the National Cyber Security Centre and Government Cyber Coordination Centre to investigate and restore services.
  • The incident follows an NCSC report of a marked rise in cyberattacks assisted by artificial intelligence since September.

Cyberattack disrupts global news distribution platform at France’s AFP — Should Read

Agence France-Presse took its AFP Forum content-distribution platform offline after a cyberattack, disrupting media clients’ access to news, photos and video. The attacker, scope of compromise, and restoration timeline remain unknown.

  • Agence France-Presse (AFP) said it was hit by a cyberattack that targeted AFP Forum, a platform clients use to browse and download its stories, photographs, and videos.
  • AFP took AFP Forum offline after detecting the intrusion and said the platform would remain unavailable until further notice.
  • AFP is investigating the incident with external cybersecurity experts and is offering subscribers alternative ways to access its content.
  • As of Friday, AFP had not identified the attacker or provided a timeline for restoring AFP Forum.
  • AFP said it remains unclear whether sensitive information was accessed or whether other AFP systems were affected.

Products: afp-forum

Vendors: agence-france-presse

A Refund Notice That Asks for Nothing Hides Its Fee Online — May Read

A Greek-language phishing email impersonating Cyprus tax authorities contained no obvious request, but its link led to a convincing refund clone that collected a tax ID and phone number while presenting a €10 processing fee. The campaign shows why email defenses must inspect landing-page behavior, not just message content or URL reputation.

  • A Greek-language email impersonating Cyprus tax authorities presented itself as a tax refund status update and included a single “Go to the Official Website” button without requesting payment, information, or urgent action in the message body.
  • The button led to a fake Cyprus tax department VAT refund page that requested a tax registration number and phone number and displayed a €10 automatic processing fee deducted from a stated €338.81 refund.
  • The identical fake refund page was hosted on two free-hosting subdomains, and link scanners returned clean verdicts for both addresses.
  • Only the first landing-page screen was captured, so the article does not claim that card data was collected or that any payment was taken.
  • The first email was reported by the recipient and moved from Junk to quarantine, while a second copy from the same sender was quarantined on arrival.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform

Products: ironscales-platform, clickfunnels

Vendors: ironscales, clickfunnels

What Happened to Binance Can Happen to Any Fortune 500 Company — Optional

Constella’s analysis of a sample of Fortune 500 companies finds that widespread employee data exposure, infostealer-compromised credentials, and third-party breaches create the same conditions exploited in the Binance attack. The report argues that security teams must monitor exposure beyond their own incidents and treat supplier and identity risk as core attack surfaces.

  • Constella analyzed 63 confirmed breaches involving 62 Fortune 500 companies in its sample and counted 2.06 billion exposed records between 2013 and 2026.
  • Twenty-seven of the 63 breaches, or 43%, were attributed to suppliers, vendors, or third-party platforms, including 18 linked to the MOVEit file-transfer campaign.
  • Across 20 randomly selected Fortune 500 companies, Constella detected 6,598,492 corporate-email exposures in a 12-month period, including 316,554 employee identities in infostealer logs from 72,733 infected devices.
  • The report states that 96.2% of employee exposure in its 20-company sample originated outside the companies' own incidents.
  • Constella reported 18 ransomware or extortion cases in its sample, including 13 confirmed cases and five additional companies listed by the n0n group in November 2026.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: moveit, snowflake, salesforce

Vendors: constella-intelligence, snowflake, salesforce

Preparing for the future AI cryptography break — Optional

Rumors of AI-driven cryptographic breakthroughs do not yet justify immediate changes, but organizations should inventory their cryptography and build algorithm agility now. This preparation will speed response to any future weakness in RSA or elliptic-curve cryptography and support migration to post-quantum, hybrid encryption.

  • Reports that AI labs may have results affecting deployed cryptography remain unconfirmed, and the article says they should be treated as a thought experiment rather than a reason for immediate changes.
  • A practical break of RSA-2048 or elliptic-curve cryptography could affect TLS connections, website certificates, and software signing, while current AI results against AES and cryptographic systems do not threaten modern deployed key sizes.
  • The article recommends that organizations create a cryptography inventory, design systems so algorithms can be replaced, and accelerate post-quantum cryptography migration using hybrid schemes where appropriate.
  • Aikido's CBOM feature is described as identifying cryptographic algorithms, protocols, and certificates in repositories, including use through libraries, while flagging weak algorithms such as MD5 and SHA-1.
  • NIST published its first post-quantum cryptography standards in August 2024, and the article states that a sufficiently capable quantum computer could also break RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography.

The vendor argues that its agent-supervised, evidence-validated approach is more suitable for production testing than self-operated ARTEX.

Health-ISAC’s daily briefing highlights escalating threats to healthcare and pharmaceutical organizations, including active exploitation of a critical Juniper flaw, Gh0stRAT campaigns, and risks from malicious use of AI and cloud-connected medical devices.

How to Keep Your Security Picture Current When Attackers Move at AI Speed — Optional

item.title: PolinRider GitHub Poisoning, GoodGuys Phishing, and Remus Gmail Theft
item.content:encoded:
Window: 26 Nov 15:00 → 26 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

North Korea-Linked PolinRider Poisons Over 7,600 GitHub Repositories to Spread Malware — Must Read

North Korea-linked PolinRider has poisoned thousands of GitHub repositories with a Python loader that retrieves its payload and C2 details from Ethereum transactions, making takedowns difficult. The campaign uses stolen developer credentials and fake job-interview lures to compromise developer machines, silently alter repositories, and distribute infostealers and backdoors.

  • PolinRider operators planted a Python loader in GitHub repositories that reads Ethereum transaction data, runs the decoded JavaScript with Node.js, and obtains command-server information from another wallet.
  • Apiiro estimated that PolinRider was present in at least 7,609 GitHub repositories owned by 2,330 accounts, with the loader pushed to 2,040 repositories between October 27 and November 6, 2026.
  • The campaign is linked to North Korean threat actors and uses fake recruitment sites, malicious packages, compromised developer machines, and stolen GitHub tokens to distribute harmful code.
  • The loader can be concealed in files such as a small utils package, conftest.py, build configuration, or VS Code auto-run tasks, and it may execute when a project is built or simply opened in VS Code.
  • Researchers found evidence of related PolinRider activity dating to February 2025, including poisoned npm packages that delivered JADESNOW, InvisibleFerret, a Socket.IO RAT, and a Python-based stealer.

Technologies: source-control, package-registry, browser

Products: github, npm, visual-studio-code, node-js, google-chrome, pypi

Vendors: github, microsoft, google, openjs-foundation

Fake paid expert interviews impersonate brands to steal Google logins — Should Read

The GoodGuys phishing campaign impersonates major brands with fake paid interview and webinar invitations to steal corporate Google and Okta credentials, then relays victims' MFA challenges to enable account takeover.

  • Push Security tracked the GoodGuys phishing campaign from October 13 and found it impersonating Accenture, American Express, Coca-Cola, Culver's, Google Cloud, Nvidia, SpaceX, and Spotify.
  • The campaign uses fake paid expert interviews, research studies, and webinars offering up to $600 to persuade recipients to sign in with work accounts.
  • Attackers distribute phishing links through legitimate email and event platforms including HireVue, SendGrid, Mandrill, and Cvent.
  • The phishing sites use attacker-controlled Google and Okta sign-in forms, reject consumer email addresses, and can request SMS codes, authenticator codes, Google number-matching prompts, or Okta Verify approvals.
  • Push Security believes the operators may manually use stolen credentials while directing the phishing pages to display the multifactor authentication challenges encountered during login.

Technologies: identity-provider, mfa, cloud-platform

Products: google-cloud, okta-verify, hirevue, sendgrid, mandrill, cvent, evilginx

Vendors: google, okta, hirevue, sendgrid, cvent

Remus malware steals Gmail messages via fake Google Sheets extension — Should Read

Remus infostealer does not exploit a Gmail zero-day; it installs a fake Google Sheets Chrome extension that repeatedly steals unread emails from signed-in Gmail accounts. The extension can persist through password changes and session revocations until the active browser session ends.

  • Researchers found that Remus’s claimed Gmail zero-day capability is implemented through a malicious Chrome extension rather than a demonstrated flaw in Gmail.
  • The extension masquerades as Google Sheets, alters the Chrome profile to register itself, and enables Developer Mode to run as an unpacked extension.
  • Once installed, it checks up to 10 signed-in Gmail accounts every minute for unread messages and sends message content, subject lines, senders, and victims’ email addresses to its command-and-control server.
  • The extension can remain installed after password changes and session revocations, but its Gmail access stops when the active browser session ends and resumes when the victim signs in again.
  • Users are advised to obtain software only from trusted sources and review chrome://extensions for unexpected extensions or Developer Mode activation.

item.title: SYS010 Malware Uses Browser Management to Spy on Gmail and Outlook
item.content:encoded:
Window: 26 Nov 11:00 → 26 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

SYS010 malware abuses browser management to spy on Gmail, Outlook — Should Read

Bitdefender reports that the SYS010 malware campaign uses malicious Meta ads for animated wallpapers to enroll browsers in attacker-controlled management and force-install extensions that steal session cookies, Meta business data, and Gmail/Outlook emails. The extensions can also delete emails, potentially hiding security alerts and intercepting account recovery codes.

  • Bitdefender tracks a SYS010 campaign that uses Meta ads for free animated wallpapers to deliver malware to Windows users.
  • The malicious apps provide the advertised animated wallpaper function while modifying Chrome, Edge, and Firefox management settings to force-install browser extensions.
  • The extensions can steal session cookies and collect Facebook Page, advertising-account, and business-account information, including spending and payment details.
  • Bitdefender found that the Chrome extension can read recent Gmail and Outlook messages, send their contents to attackers, and permanently delete selected emails.
  • Bitdefender recommends avoiding software downloads from social-media ads and refusing administrator prompts whose purpose is unclear.

Technologies: browser, operating-system

Products: chrome, edge, firefox, gmail, outlook, windows, meta-ads

Vendors: bitdefender, meta, google, microsoft, mozilla
